_readme: Copy this file to agents.json and describe your own Fabric data agents.
agents.json is gitignored. For hosting, put the same JSON in the HALO_AGENTS
environment variable instead, so your GUIDs never enter the repo.
url         paste the whole MCP endpoint from the data agent's Endpoints page
description what the agent DOES hold, phrased positively. The classifier routes
on this alone, so it is the single most important field here.
excludes    what it does not hold. Only the model sees this; keeping it out of
description matters, because the no-model keyword fallback is a bag
of words and would index 'customer' against an agent whose
description said 'no customer data'.
Writing good descriptions:
1. Name concrete nouns a user would actually type (plants, invoices, sellers),
not abstractions (metrics, insights, data).
2. Make them disjoint. If two agents both say 'revenue', say whose revenue:
subscription revenue versus physical product revenue.
3. State the data range if it is unusual, so cross-domain answers can be
honest about differing periods.
4. Put definitions in description, not excludes. 'Turbomachinery never
includes motors' read to a classifier as 'holds no motor data', and
questions about motors got refused.
5. Run `python probe_agents.py` and write these from what it prints, rather
than from what you assume the agent contains.
Delete this _readme key in your own file.
examples: How many orders were placed last month?
Compare order volume with production output

sales.description: Sales and orders. Customers, accounts, orders and order lines, products and categories, discounts, order revenue, cost and margin, sales territories and reps. This is the source for booked commercial revenue.
sales.excludes: Nothing from the factory floor: no plants, lines, machines, OEE, scrap, yield, downtime or production quantity.

manufacturing.description: Manufacturing operations. Plants, production lines, machinery and assets, production quantity, OEE, scrap rate, yield, downtime minutes and downtime reasons or root causes, and inventory on hand.
manufacturing.excludes: No customer-level data, no vendors or purchasing, no employees, and nothing about commercial orders or booked revenue.
